text:
emma-support: Hey team — NovusPay (acct 99984) raised a dispute: Dec invoice INV-202312-99984 shows ~1,920,412 tokens billed but their dashboard total for Dec is 1,235,000. Customer says no spike on their end. Invoice has an extra line labeled 'dedicated-fallback' ~685k tokens. Can anyone quickly sanity-check?

leo-eng: Can you paste invoice line IDs and the billing run ts? I can look at routing logs.

emma-support: invoice_id INV-202312-99984, billing_run 2023-12-31-23:59Z, line_id 42d9-fallback-99984. Customer screenshot attached in ticket.

sam-devex: quick repro queries you can run (runs against internal metering DB):
```
-- tokens counted by source and partition for account 99984 in Dec
SELECT source, SUM(tokens) as tokens_total
FROM metering.events
WHERE account_id = 99984
  AND event_ts >= '2023-12-01'
  AND event_ts < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY source;
```
This should show if billing pipeline got events tagged as fallback/dedicated.

dev-billing: I pulled the billing pipeline for that invoice: there are ~685,412 tokens with reason = "dedicated_fallback" and routed_at = '2023-12-31T23:58:47Z'. Those events were ingested by the billing job AFTER the dashboard's month-end snapshot (snapshot taken 2023-12-31T23:45:00Z). Looks like a late backfill from capacity fallback.

dev-billing: snippet from billing queue index: `{"acct":99984, "tokens":685412, "reason":"dedicated_fallback", "job_id":"backfill-309876", "ingest_ts":"2024-01-01T00:05:12Z"}`

anna-finance: So invoice reflects post-cutoff ingested tokens (billing pipeline accepted them) but dashboard snapshot excluded them. That explains the ~685k gap. Do we have a policy for backfills that land after snapshot?

ingest-bot: backfill job completed: job_id=backfill-309876, triggered_by=dedicated-queue-surge, completed_at=2024-01-01T00:05:12Z, produced_tokens=685412, target_account=99984. Logs: `wrote 685412 events to billing-topic`

leo-eng: Confirming hypothesis: dashboard snapshots are taken at X, billing pipeline consumes real-time stream and the backfill wrote historical events with ingest_ts after snapshot but billed in run because billing run uses ingestion order. Two options: (1) Issue invoice credit for the backfilled tokens OR (2) re-run dashboard snapshot to include backfilled events and communicate adjusted totals to customer.

sam-devex: short-term remediation steps: 1) For this customer propose a credit for 685,412 tokens (or prorated $) while we investigate; 2) Add a reconciliation job that compares billing-topic vs dashboard-snapshot deltas at +24h and flags >1% differences; 3) Tag backfill events with original event_ts and a backfill_flag so dashboards can optionally include them when showing historical month totals.

emma-support: I'll propose credit and send a short explanation: "We found a backfill to the billing pipeline that landed after the dashboard snapshot for the month-close; billing included it, dashboard didn't. We're issuing a one-time credit while we adjust backfill tagging and reconciliation." Will copy finance for approval.

anna-finance: Please include the exact token count and invoice line reference; I'll approve a credit memo for INV-202312-99984 if dev-billing confirms numbers.

dev-billing: Confirmed: 685412 tokens, line_id 42d9-fallback-99984, job_id backfill-309876.

leo-eng: Postmortem items: doc the backfill timing guarantees, ensure backfills either: (a) re-index dashboards with original timestamps, or (b) flow through a reconciliation pipeline so billing and dashboards converge before invoice finalization. Also add an alert when backfills > 100k tokens land within 2h of month-end.

emma-support: Thanks all — updating NovusPay with proposed credit and ETA for follow-up. Will circle back here after finance OK. :white_check_mark:
